title: George Lewis, Lee Collins, Earl Humphrey and their wives

blocks.x: Was George Lewis old fashioned and good boy with that old time in him?

Yeah, he was old fashioned. And you see like this boy played with Thomas would play with Celestan. All that, he was more modern than all of them because he couldn't read but he was nice coming up, but all of them, they come back and shawky, Banana brought back that. René used to teach shawky, you understand, you didn't know that did you?

No, René used to teach shawky. You see, Lee Collins, Lee Collins was playing up there after Lewis and them left at the Beverly Gardens up there and Lee Collins and Earl Humphrey and all of them used to play together. He used to live down there in Belmont Place, let me tell you a joke about Earl Humphrey and Lee Collins and they left a dance one night, the Beverly Gardens didn't go on, you know the dance didn't go on, they come home. Well they wise, they had two guys entertain them, serenading, drinking wine and stuff out them big old boys from the pitchers, you understand, and they come home and the guys went and got up underneath the house with the guitars you know. And Earl said Lee, he said Lee, why do you think we didn't work? He said, we're modeling and the pretty chance of all we probably worked by winning. He said, well something is wrong. He said, what do you mean? He said, it sounds like I hear music. Some guys with them guitars got hung up with them nails up underneath the house. Well I used to kiddo about that before he died, Willie's brother. Yeah. His wife was named Unesteemed Netterville at that time. He married and Lee Collins' wife was named, what was her name?
Can't think of, well the one in Chicago was Mary, wasn't it? That was his last wife.

Yeah. But he had a wife before her, Lillian. Lillian was the wife, Lillian. That was the last, that's the woman who looked out for him, she used to book him when he was down there at Paddock, I believe.
Lee Collins' you talking about? Yeah. He was down there, yeah he was down there, William and on and all that bunch. Want me to bring you some coke? No it's okay.
